Ubuntu is the most widely used Linux distribution in the world, delivering kernels across a vast matrix of versions, architectures, and configurations – with up to 15 years of security and maintenance commitments for Long Term Support (LTS) releases. You will build and evolve automated test frameworks – including stress testing, fuzzing, code coverage analysis, and regression detection – that not only must remain effective across many concurrently supported kernel versions spanning years of maintenance, but must be able to scale with the high demand for Ubuntu kernels (currently more than 160 under active support).
The successful candidate will bring strong Python skills, familiarity with Linux kernel internals, and experience building test infrastructure that scales. You will work closely with kernel engineers to catch regressions early, validate fixes, and ensure every kernel we ship meets the highest standards of reliability.

Measure and improve kernel code coverage, identifying gaps in test coverage and creating tests to address them

We are seeking a skilled and motivated Software Quality Engineer to join our Mission Assurance team. This role sits at the intersection where software quality meets in-orbit operations, offering the opportunity to drive the operational performance of a satellite constellation.

The role has two facets, you will own software quality assurance activities across the development lifecycle and also provide quality oversight to the team operating our constellation of satellites during commissioning, operations, and anomaly response.

As the company implements its development roadmap, the distinction between these two aspects will blur with satellite operations increasingly transitioning to automated AI/ML tools to manage the fleet.
The ideal candidate combines a rigorous, process-driven approach to software quality with an analytical mindset and operational awareness to allow them to ensure on-orbit anomalies are investigated and resolved effectively.
This is a broad remit, so previous experience in both areas is not required. For example, a strong software QA background in a demanding industry (e.g. banking, medical, defence) will likely also have developed the analytical mindset needed to investigate on orbit issues.

You will work closely with a fantastic team of software engineers, systems engineers, technical experts and spacecraft operators to ensure that our software and satellites are fit for purpose and that deviations from expected behaviour are understood, reported, assessed, and resolved with sound engineering judgment.
What You’ll Do as Software & Satellite Operations Quality Engineer:

Define and maintain software QA processes, standards, and acceptance criteria for onboard and ground segment software across the full development lifecycle.
Ensure that software verification and validation activities are comprehensive and correctly executed.
Ensure the Software Development Lifecycle meets applicable quality requirements and standards.
Where situations require deviation from defined process, ensure that this is performed safely and in a controlled manner.
Raise, track, and manage non-conformances, ensuring corrective and preventive actions are identified and implemented effectively.
Ensure risks are identified, evaluated and communicated effectively to the project and management team.
Ensure that the software configuration baseline is maintained throughout development and mission lifetimes.
Confirm all software releases are reviewed and compliant to standards.
Contribute to process improvement initiatives and ensure compliance with applicable standards (e.g. ISO 29110, ECSS-Q-ST-80, ECSS-E-ST-40, or equivalent).

Provide Mission Assurance support to satellite operations, especially during critical mission phases such as Checkout and Commissioning, In-Orbit Verification and anomaly response.
Lead and contribute to anomaly investigations, root cause analyses, and failure review boards, ensuring findings are well-documented and lessons are captured.
Ensure the mission impact of anomalies is assessed and operational workarounds, corrective actions and recovery steps are appropriate.
Identify links between incidents and coordinate response to common anomalies across the fleet.
Ensure lessons learned are fed back to satellite development teams using non-conformance and corrective action processes.
Liaise with software development, systems engineering and satellite operations teams to continually improve satellite operations tooling, improving Fault Detection, Isolation and Recovery (FDIR), increasing automation and raising the availability of the satellite fleet through transition to AI/ML based systems.
Serve as the mission assurance interface to the operations team, software engineers, and systems engineers during anomaly investigations and resolution.

BSc or MEng in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
3+ years of experience in a software QA, systems engineering, or mission assurance role within a highly regulated industry (e.g. aerospace, defence, banking, medical).
Proven track record of contributing to investigations and fault finding of complex systems.
Familiarity with version control systems (e.g. Git) and issue tracking tools.
Understanding of software development lifecycles (Agile and/or waterfall) and associated QA activities.
Clear and concise communicator, able to present technical findings to diverse audiences including management and non-specialist stakeholders.

Experience working with FMEA, FDIR, hazard analysis, or other dependability and safety analysis methods.
Experience with satellite operations or ground segment software in an operational environment.
Experience supporting LEOP, commissioning, or in-orbit validation activities.
Proficiency in scripting or data analysis for telemetry analysis.
Background in configuration management in a regulated engineering environment.
Experience with failure review boards or anomaly resolution in an operational setting.
Knowledge of relevant standards such as ISO 29110, ECSS-Q-ST-80, ECSS-E-ST-40, or DO-178C.

In short
If you're a Senior QA Engineer who's tested apps that talk to physical devices, and you know that "reproduce on my phone" doesn't end the conversation, we want to talk. You'd join us on a freelance, time & material basis : you're paid for the hours you actually work on real client projects.

The first three months are about figuring out if we're a good match. When things work out, and that depends on the work itself, the project pipeline, and business timing, there's a real path to our core team with a permanent contract and full benefits.
Why intent ?
We've been designing and co-creating connected devices since 2008. Wearables, smart audio, health-tech hardware for clients like Oura and BOSE, backed by investors like a16z and Founders Fund. We're 60+ people, fully remote, and AI-native since before LinkedIn influencers discovered the term.

Our QA isn't "check the screens": it's a mobile app talking to firmware over BLE, sometimes with a flaky signal, sometimes at the edge of battery, sometimes on a phone that decided to update overnight. The bugs are real, the details matter, and good QA changes whether a product ships well or limps out the door.
Who this role is NOT for
If you like running the same test pass every sprint and closing tickets the moment the build is green, we're probably not your people. We look for QA who ask "why" before "how", challenge specs that don't add up, and dig into firmware logs when something smells off. We're AI-native and we expect you to treat AI as a daily multiplier, not a gimmick.

What we expect: ownership of what you touch, straight talk when something is wrong, and the kind of curiosity that makes you actually care about the device, not just the app on top of it.

Compatibility testing: make sure devices, sensors, gateways, protocols, and platforms actually play well together
Functional testing: data collection, storage, processing, real-time monitoring, control, integrations
Performance testing: behavior under different workloads, networks, and physical conditions, finding bottlenecks and latency
Security testing: vulnerabilities in devices, communication protocols, transmission, storage, access, auth
Mentor less experienced testers, raise the bar on QA practices
Take part in requirement discussions and daily calls, flag inconsistencies and open issues early
Share knowledge inside the QA chapter and across the company
Use AI tools as part of your daily workflow, not as a party trick
How we work
Fully remote. We have a pet-friendly office in Warsaw and a coworking space in Gdansk if walls and coffee machines motivate you, but nobody will ask why you're not there. Working hours are flexible: most of the team operates between 10:00 and 18:00 CET, and that's when most meetings happen.

Evening calls with US-based clients (up to ~20:00) are part of the rhythm, sometimes a couple of times a week, always planned ahead. You'll be part of the QA chapter for knowledge-sharing, and at the same time on a project squad led by a PM for day-to-day delivery.
What you'll get

s.h: Truly flexible hours: you organize your day
s.t:
Fully remote, with pet-friendly Warsaw office + Gdansk cowork if you want them
Access to our internal knowledge-sharing: tech talks, experiments, side projects
When the first 3 months work out, and that depends on the work, the project pipeline, and business timing, there's a real path to a permanent contract with a fixed monthly salary, 26 days paid leave, 10 sick days, Saltus medical care, and a training budget
No sugarcoating: during the freelance period there's no paid leave or medical benefits. Those come with the permanent contract, and we're transparent about that upfront.
Your first weeks
We aim to give you space to ramp up before jumping into live project work, but this is a real company with real deadlines: if the project needs you sooner, we'll make sure you have the support to hit the ground running. You'll get paired with a buddy and tackle progressively bigger tasks, so both sides can see how the collaboration feels.

Feedback comes early and often, no one waits three months to tell you something isn't working. If it's great, you'll know. If something needs adjusting, you'll hear about it while there's still time to adjust.
Recruitment process
The entire process is in English. All interviews are recorded for internal evaluation purposes.
Application with a few screening questions
HR call, ~45 min, casual
Technical meeting, ~90 min, with the QA team
Final feedback within a few days
Once we're in touch, you'll hear from us fast. We don't ghost and we don't drag.
One more thing
intent is an equal opportunity employer. We care about what you can do, not where you come from. Send us your CV and a few words about why this caught your eye. Bonus points if you share a bug you found that nobody else would have.

s.h: ABOUT US METYCLE - where innovation meets sustainability
s.t:
We are building the B2B online platform to accelerate the global circular flow of secondary metals. By connecting buyers and sellers of scrap metal globally, we enable efficient trade of secondary metals and drive the seamless flow of recycling material, essential for reducing CO2 emissions by up to 95% compared to primary metal production.
And we take it further! We are pioneering an innovative Smart Sorting Facility that leverages AI, machine learning, and robotics to transform how scrap metal is processed, enhance material quality, improve traceability, and drive the recycling industry into the digital era.
Join us at the early stage in bringing the $610 billion scrap metal trading industry into the 21st century and in shaping the future of metal recycling and green energy solutions.
READY TO MAKE AN IMPACT? If you are passionate about industrial automation, solving complex technical challenges, and building something from the ground up, join our team as an Industrial Automation Engineer.
The machinery is the easy part to buy. The control system that turns it into a plant - and the standards, documentation, and data that keep it running - is what we are hiring you to own.
We are looking for an experienced Industrial Automation Engineer to take ownership of our plant’s control systems from design through commissioning and into stable production. You bring deep hands-on experience in programming and commissioning industrial control systems and are comfortable taking responsibility for the PLC, safety systems, HMI, industrial networking, and interfaces between multiple machine suppliers.
Beyond programming, you understand what it takes to make a plant genuinely reliable in production and have the technical confidence to hold suppliers to high professional standards. Join our international team, help build innovative solutions for scrap metal processing, and contribute to a more sustainable future.
YOUR MISSION PLC & Plant Control: Design, write, and own the PLC program using Siemens TIA Portal / S7-1200 & S7-1500, including control logic, sequencing, fault handling, and HMI
Commissioning & Production: Take the plant from design through commissioning to a stable, running line, owning the full journey through FAT/SAT and the hands-on work required to make the plant genuinely reliable
Plant Availability: Design stop and interlock behaviour to minimise unnecessary downtime — allowing unaffected parts of the plant to keep running when it is safe to do so. Plant availability is a direct business outcome here, and you will directly influence it
Machine Safety: Implement the machine-safety control concept on a fail-safe F-CPU with F-I/O, including the hardwired e-stop loop, PLC-enforced zone isolation that cannot be overridden, guard interlocks, and controlled, sequenced shutdown
Safety & Compliance: Be our in-house technical counterpart on EN ISO 13849 performance-level determination and the CE file, working with external assessors while retaining ownership of the technical approach and decisions
Machine Integration: Integrate control systems from several different machine suppliers into one coherent line, so that a single stop is genuinely a single stop across the whole plant
Supplier Management: Hold machine builders and panel builders to specification, including unlocked code, complete documentation, and standards compliance
OT / IT & Industrial IoT: Get plant data out over OPC UA / MQTT / Modbus TCP into our own systems, so stoppage reasons, energy use, and throughput become actionable data. Work closely with our Industrial IoT team, who own the edge and data side of that boundary
YOUR PROFILE 5+ years of hands-on experience programming and commissioning industrial control systems, with a track record of bringing production equipment or complete lines into stable operation
Deep Siemens TIA Portal / S7-1200 & S7-1500 experience, with strong skills in SCL, LAD/FBD, HMI/SCADA, industrial networking (PROFINET, PROFIBUS, Modbus TCP), drives/VFDs, and fault-finding
Strong machine safety competence, including F-CPU / Safety Integrated and EN ISO 13849, with the ability to explain and defend performance-level determinations
Comfortable reading electrical schematics and troubleshooting cabinets, hardware, signals, wiring, and control behaviour directly on the shop floor. You have brought at least one production line from commissioning into stable production; maintenance-only experience is not sufficient
Experience working with machine and panel builders, with the confidence to hold suppliers accountable for code quality, documentation, standards compliance, and professional delivery
Experience with brownfield projects and legacy migration (STEP 7 Classic → TIA); experience in bulk material handling, recycling, sorting, or minerals processing is a plus
Experience with PLC version control, simulation / digital twins, or structured automation approaches is desirable. Additional IT/OT skills such as Python, C#/TIA Openness, SQL, Linux, Docker, MES/IIoT, OT network segmentation, or IEC 62443 are a plus
Independent, structured, and hands-on, with a strong sense of ownership. You challenge assumptions, hold suppliers to a high standard, and document what you build
Fluent in English; German and/or Dutch is a plus. Ideally based in or near Cologne or the Benelux/border region, with valid EU work authorisation and the willingness to travel to our Smart Sorting Facility in Belgium, Maasmechelen
WHY JOIN US? You will have the opportunity to challenge the status quo and work on an innovative venture with a significant impact
You will be able to take ownership and shape the future of metal recycling and green energy solutions at an early stage

Founded in 2017, RoomPriceGenie is dedicated to helping hoteliers around the globe achieve optimal pricing. 🌍 We understand that many small hotels face challenges with digitalization, making their operations increasingly complex and often resulting in lost revenue. This is where we come in!
We have developed a powerful solution that enables hotels to set the right prices in just seconds. ⏱️ Our state-of-the-art algorithm analyzes both internal hotel data and market trends to recommend pricing strategies that enhance revenue and improve booking rates.
With customers spanning the globe—from the USA and Canada to Iceland, South Africa, China, Slovenia, Italy, and the UK—RoomPriceGenie has made a meaningful impact in the hospitality industry, and our clients love the results. ❤️
Now, we are excited to expand our customer base and spread the word about how we can support hoteliers in optimizing their pricing strategies. We invite you to join us on this journey! We actively encourage applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds to enrich our team and drive innovation.
Why RoomPriceGenie?
We take both culture and product seriously: recognized as Best Place to Work in HotelTech (2026) and Best Revenue Management Software (2026) . We power pricing for thousands of hotels worldwide on a modern data stack.
This is a fully remote role within Europe (UTC+0 to UTC+2) . You will have genuine ownership, strong support, and the opportunity to build high-value internal AI systems and agents that make our operational teams significantly faster and smarter.

As an AI Systems & Automation Engineer , you will drive internal AI adoption across Customer Success, Sales, and Operations. Your job isn't to build raw ML models or write throwaway demos. You will work directly with business leads to unblock legacy processes, connect internal data to core operational tools, and deploy dependable, supervised AI agents that automate complex workflows.
You will join our AI & Security team and bridge the gap between our core data platforms (Snowflake, Postgres, DocumentDB, S3) and our GTM stack (HubSpot, Chargebee, Modjo, Notion), establishing practical patterns for safe, agentic automation across the business.

Translate Business Pain into Systems: Partner directly with Customer Success, Sales, and Ops teams to map out manual, multi-step workflows and design high-ROI AI automation targets.
Build Production Agents & Integrations: Write clean, maintainable code (Python/TypeScript) connecting LLM APIs to internal data stores and third-party SaaS platforms (HubSpot, Chargebee, Modjo, Notion).
Implement Modern Agent Standards: Build modular agent capabilities using standardized tools and schemas (such as Agent Skills standards, Claude Plugins, or custom function-calling pipelines) to give models safe, structured action boundaries.
Design Human-in-the-Loop Workflows: Implement strict guardrails, schema validation, human approval gates, and escalation paths so non-technical staff can safely supervise AI outputs.
Ensure Integration Reliability: Manage API rate limits, Webhooks, asynchronous jobs, and retry logic to keep integrations rock-solid as internal data volume grows.
Measure & Iterate: Build lightweight evaluation harnesses to track agent accuracy, hallucination rates, latency, and cost, optimizing prompt architectures and model choices based on real production usage.
Your Profile
Strong Software Fundamentals: Solid background in Python and/or TypeScript, asynchronous execution, REST APIs, Webhooks, SQL, and working with relational or analytical databases.
Claude & LLM Ecosystem Expertise: Deep, hands-on proficiency with Claude (Anthropic API, Prompt Engineering, Workbench, SDKs) and adjacent modern developer applications.
Agent Skill & Tool Design: Familiarity with modern agent capability frameworks, such as standard Agent Skills ( agentskills.io ), Claude Plugins / Model Context Protocol (MCP), or structured tool execution design.
Integration & Ecosystem Familiarity: Experience consuming complex SaaS APIs (HubSpot, Chargebee, Modjo). Proficiency with Notion (APIs, workspace structures, and knowledge management) is a strong plus.
Operational Empathy: Business-minded engineer who enjoys talking to non-technical colleagues, understanding messy legacy processes, and building practical tools that make their daily jobs easier.
Location & Communication: Fluent in English and based in European time zones (UTC+0 to UTC+2).

s.h: MAIN PURPOSE OF THE ROLE & RESPONSIBILITIES IN THE BUSINESS
s.t:
As a Lead Test Engineer (Consultant) in Kainos , you’ll be a technical leader and innovator in software testing, providing strong test leadership and direction within a multi-skilled agile team, within the public, defence or healthcare sector.

Taking responsibility for the strategy, design and development of automated, manual, and non-functional tests, you’ll help the team to deliver working application software that meets user needs and is of sufficient quality for promotion to users. It’s a fast-paced environment so it is important for you to make sound, reasoned decisions.

You’ll do this whilst learning about new technologies and approaches, with talented colleagues who will help you learn, develop and grow.
You’ll manage, coach and develop a small number of staff, with a focus on managing employee performance and assisting in their career development. You’ll also provide direction and leadership for your team as you solve challenging problems together.
As a technical leader in the team, you will also interact with customers, share knowledge and mentor those around you.

Experience of ensuring testing layers have adequate coverage in line with software testing principles and practices.
Expertise in designing, creating and maintaining tests scripts and test approaches, including manual and automated testing across all layers of an application including non-functional test coverage.
Experience using Test Automation open-source technologies (e.g. one of the following Selenium, JUnit,TestNG, Cucumber, Cypress), and configuring tools for testing such as Jenkins and/or TeamCity, within a continuous integration environment.
Practical knowledge of at least one object-oriented programming language (e.g. Java).
A high level of technical awareness and a sound understanding of software architectures.
We are passionate about developing people – experience in managing others, setting objectives, giving feedback and leading performance reviews.
Passionate technologist, keen to expand knowledge of latest QA tools, tech and methodologies.

Operating within a Test Lead role (or similar) on a medium-large sized Agile project.
Demonstrable experience of effective stakeholder management and commercial awareness.
Experience within defence, health or public sectors
